studies.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for the Navigation of Neurovascular Catheters
studies.robot_used: Fraunhofer IPA experimental robotic manipulator for the two DOF of a guidewire: maximum linear travel 300 mm, infinite rotation (Sec. 2.4); guidewire only, no catheter; overhead camera, MeVisLab tracking (Sec. 2.3)
studies.simulator: SOFA + BeamAdapter; rigid vessel walls, wall-guidewire friction 0.1, empty lumen (no dynamic resistance) (Sec. 2.2)
studies.trained: policy (DDPG, with HER and human demonstrations as options, OpenAI Baselines; DQN with double Q-learning, dueling networks, prioritised replay, RLlib) (Sec. 2.1); only DDPG ran on the test bench (Sec. 2.5)
studies.observation: absolute guidewire tip coordinates, the target and the manipulator rotation (Sec. 2.1); on the bench, tip from an overhead camera registered to a CT of the phantom, threshold segmentation and centreline (Sec. 2.3)
studies.action_space: DDPG: continuous translation and rotation; DQN: discrete, 8 combinations of the two DOF (Sec. 2.1)
studies.gap_closing: none described; 'The simulation does not yet include noise and latency' (Sec. 3)
studies.real_setup: idealised PMMA phantom, constant 10 mm vessel diameter, a bifurcation followed by a bi- and trifurcation in one plane, water-filled; random start and target; 10 bench runs (Sec. 2.4, 3, Fig. 3)
studies.sim_success: DDPG + HER 89.6% (sparse reward), DQN + Rainbow 86.5% (dense reward), average success rates; SD over four training attempts 4.4% and 6.2%; plain DDPG 83.1%, DDPG + HER + HD 87.9% (Sec. 3, Figs. 4-5); episodes per evaluation N.R.
studies.real_success: 7/10 (the trained DDPG model on the test bench) (Sec. 3)
studies.gap_measure: 89.6% -> 70% (7/10), reading the transferred 'trained DDPG model' as the DDPG + HER of the same paragraph; failed attempts 'happened at junctions, where exact state data is necessary' (Sec. 3)
studies.notes: Primary read 2026-11-08: not simulation-only. The two reviews did not disagree: Robertshaw 2023 (70% DDPG) gives the bench result and Sun 2025 (86.5% DQN / 89.6% DDPG) the simulated one. Same 2-DOF manipulator, camera tracking and simulation framework that karstensen2020_autonomous 'reused'. Planar idealised phantom, guidewire only.

studies.title: Automatic control of cardiac ablation catheter with deep reinforcement learning method
studies.robot_used: tendon-driven steerable EP-catheter robot, 3 motors (translation, rotation, distal bending); TactiCath Quartz catheter; Aurora EM tracker (Fig. 1)
studies.simulator: Unity (catheter + heart collision model; rendered to angiography-like images)
studies.observation: two 256x256 simulated angiography images (previous + current step) plus tip and goal positions; on hardware tip from EM, image rendered from EM positions
studies.action_space: discrete, 8 actions (translate 1 mm, rotate 3 deg, bend 1 deg)
studies.gap_closing: randomised insertion angle and action magnitude (two noise types)
studies.real_setup: printed rigid right-atrium phantom, 100 episodes per model
studies.gap_measure: success 98% -> 73% without randomisation; 96% -> 87% with both noise types (S7b Table S7b2; paper Table 2)
studies.notes: Intracardiac, tendon-driven catheter, not a neurovascular guidewire robot. Earliest simulation-to-robot study in the S7b set that measures a gap with and without randomisation.

studies.title: Autonomous guidewire navigation in a two dimensional vascular phantom
studies.robot_used: Fraunhofer IPA guidewire manipulator, 2 DOF (translation, rotation), 'reused' from behr2019_deep; gamepad for manual override; camera above and light source below the phantom emulating fluoroscopy, 5 Hz (Materials and methods, Fig. 1)
studies.simulator: SOFA + BeamAdapter; phantom walls rigid, lumen empty; wall friction and guidewire stiffness iteratively tuned to mimic guidewire failure in the test bench (Materials and methods)
studies.observation: five guidewire points 5 mm apart from the tip (XZ) for the current and last three time steps, plus the last three actions (Materials and methods); on the bench from the camera image at 5 Hz; target coordinates given to the network (interim-target test)
studies.action_space: continuous translation and rotation commands; control at 5 Hz
studies.gap_closing: friction and guidewire stiffness tuned to reproduce the bench failure (entanglement at bifurcations); on the bench, the next bifurcation given as interim target
studies.real_setup: rigid 2D phantom, stereolithography print, filled with glycerine-water; a loop that forces a detour and a bifurcation that needs translation and rotation together (Fig. 2); random start and target; number of bench episodes N.R.
studies.sim_success: maximum 96% after 52,500 training episodes (100 test episodes every 500 training episodes; success = target within 25 s) (Materials and methods, Results, Fig. 3)
studies.real_success: 'the same results as navigating in the simulation environment' (no number, episodes N.R.); 100% with the next bifurcation as interim target, evaluated 'to improve the success rate on the testbench' (Materials and methods, Results)
studies.gap_measure: none stated: bench reported equal to simulation without a count; failures of the fully trained controller are path-choice (high-level) failures only (Results)
studies.notes: Second Fraunhofer bench study: same manipulator, camera tracking and simulation framework as behr2019_deep. First statement of the friction-and-stiffness tuning procedure later quoted from karstensen2022_learning. The bench success is a verbal statement, so fig_sim2real (b) draws no line for it.

studies.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Image-Based Autonomous Guidewire Navigation Trained by Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient with Behavior Cloning for Fast Learning
studies.robot_used: bench guidewire controller (translation + rotation) under overhead camera (Fig. 8); no robot name
studies.simulator: SOFA (virtual planar vessel map)
studies.trained: policy (DDPG after behaviour cloning from a rule-based expert)
studies.observation: four stacked 128x128 3-channel images centred on tip (vessel mask, centreline, guidewire centreline) plus 4 previous actions; same hand-written image processing in both domains
studies.action_space: continuous: translate up to 0.8 mm, rotate up to 30 deg per step
studies.gap_closing: image reduced to masks in both domains; image rotation, shift 0.2, scale 0.7-1 augmentation
studies.real_setup: planar phantom of a different shape, camera 30 Hz, 4 targets x 10 episodes
studies.gap_measure: none (same or better; real vessel differs from sim vessel)
studies.notes: Easiest transfer in the set: 2D planar map, image abstracted to masks, camera pose fixed. Real-vessel shape differs from training map, so it also tests geometry generalisation.

studies.title: A Simulation Framework for Magnetic Continuum Robots
studies.robot_used: magnetic continuum robot, 1.5 mm (4.5 Fr) OD, three NdFeB ring magnets, pushed by a remote-controlled advancer and steered by a pre-clinical eMNS of 3 coils on a triangular base, up to 25 mT (Sec. III-A, III-B, Fig. 3)
studies.simulator: SOFA + BeamAdapter (1D Kirchhoff-rod FEM, Lagrange-multiplier contact, Coulomb friction 0.01 in validation, Sec. III-E) coupled through ROS to a multipole model of the eMNS field, b(p) = A(p) i; advancer enters as the user insertion speed (Sec. II-A, II-B, Fig. 4)
studies.observation: Tip position and pointing angle (camera markers on the bench; simulated tip in SOFA)
studies.action_space: Recorded field and advancer inputs of a user, replayed open loop
studies.gap_closing: Young's moduli swept by hand in an obstacle-free calibration model; friction tuned by hand (Sec. III-F, V)
studies.real_setup: planar, 4 mm high, rigid POM and PMMA models (calibration, vasculature-like, free-form); Canon EOS 6D camera (Sec. III-C, III-D)
studies.real_success: mean tip position error 5.1 to 6.8 mm and orientation error 3.8 to 7.2 deg over the three models (phantom); per-way-point errors in Table II
studies.gap_measure: tip position and orientation error between real and simulated device over the whole navigation (Sec. III-G, V)
studies.notes: Simulated vs physical device without a controller: belongs in Table VIII(c). Models the field source of a magnetic device but not the advancer (no slip); rigid vessels, no blood flow, no image rendering (RViz only). eMNS not named in the paper; no catalogue row attached.

studies.title: Learning-based autonomous vascular guidewire navigation without human demonstration in the venous system of a porcine liver
studies.robot_used: customised guidewire manipulator (continuous rotation; translation up to 300 mm) under C-arm fluoroscopy
studies.simulator: SOFA + BeamAdapter (rigid wall, empty lumen; 0.035 in Terumo Radifocus angled stiff guidewire)
studies.trained: policy (deep RL, controller with recurrent layers; algorithm not re-checked); perception was a separate recurrent-CNN tracker
studies.observation: 5 tip points 1 mm apart in 2D; on hardware from real 7.5 fps fluoroscopy through recurrent-CNN tracker (error ~1.3 mm); tracking delay modelled as normal, mean 0.13 s
studies.action_space: continuous translation + rotation of the wire base
studies.gap_closing: friction and wire stiffness hand-tuned to mimic the test bench; tracking delay in training
studies.real_setup: ex vivo porcine liver (one organ; CT mesh from the same liver) with pump flow; 10 targets per main vein
studies.gap_measure: -70 points; failure split wrong branch 33.3%, entanglement 36.6% (Table 1); authors blame soft-tissue registration for wrong-branch failures
studies.notes: First learned controller in S7b run under real fluoroscopy. Largest measured drop. Rigid wall in sim vs compliant liver vessels in reality is the unmodelled difference.

studies.title: Learning-based autonomous navigation, benchmark environments and simulation framework for endovascular interventions
studies.robot_used: custom guidewire manipulator: stepper rotating the wire directly (infinite rotation) on a linear rail driven by a second stepper (300 mm); housing labelled "guido" in Fig. 4
studies.simulator: stEVE / SOFA BeamAdapter; stEVE_bench BasicWireNav, ArchVariety, DualDeviceNav
studies.observation: 3 tip points in 2D, current + previous, target, last action; hardware: overhead-camera tracker (transparent phantom) or fluoroscopy tracker
studies.action_space: continuous translation (35 mm/s) and rotation (3.14 rad/s) per device, 7.5 Hz
studies.gap_closing: hand-tuned friction and stiffness (Karstensen 2022 procedure); ArchVariety randomises arch shape and scale 0.7-1.3
studies.real_setup: 3D-printed rigid aortic arch phantoms; camera bench 100+100 trials, fluoroscopy 10 trials

studies.notes: Smallest gap in the set, on a rigid phantom with one wire and tracked-tip observation. Fig. 4 left = camera bench, right = fluoroscopy bench; simulation views are Fig. 2 and Fig. 5 (not cropped).

studies.title: FreezeSeg2RL: Frozen Segmentation Pretraining for Reinforcement Learning On Vascular Interventional Robot Autonomous Delivering

studies.title: Sim2Real Learning With Domain Randomization for Autonomous Guidewire Navigation in Robotic-Assisted Endovascular Procedures
studies.robot_used: vascular intervention robot of United Imaging Research Institute of Intelligent Imaging (Fig. 3, C-arm and table)
studies.simulator: SOFA 23.06 + BeamAdapter; one 0.9 mm guidewire (density 1.55 g/cm3)
studies.trained: policy (PPO + GAE + domain randomisation; SAC, DDPG baselines)
studies.observation: sim: tip position, velocity, curvature, orientation, tip force, vessel diameter; robot: not described (no real-time position feedback needed)
studies.action_space: insertion, two rotations, torque increment (discrete set)
studies.gap_closing: domain randomisation: friction uniform [0.1, 0.5] and tissue elasticity [0.5, 2.0] kPa per episode; GAE
studies.real_setup: simplified vascular phantom with physical twin; 4-5 trials per method; 2 human operators x 3
studies.sim_success: PPO 7/10 and 8/10; PPO+DR 8/10 and 9/10; PPO+GAE+DR 9/10 and 9/10 (targets A, B)

studies.notes: Only study in the set that randomises friction and wall elasticity. Second crop yao2025_sim2real_sim.png shows the simulated tasks (Fig. 2). Policy runs near open loop.

studies.title: From Patient-Specific Digital Twin to Real-World Phantom: Autonomous Right Heart Catheterization
studies.robot_used: custom 2-DoF Swan-Ganz catheter robot: active-passive roller set with soft silicone layers (translation) + rotation stage with slip ring (continuous rotation); Aurora EM balloon calibration; RealSense camera
studies.simulator: SOFA + BeamAdapter patient-specific digital twin (phantom E 10 kPa, nu 0.49, density 1.2 g/cm3, Rayleigh damping 0.1/0.1); Swan-Ganz catheter beam model
studies.trained: policy by supervised learning (CNN decision model, behaviour cloning of user key-press controller; 150 virtual trials, 50 per phantom)
studies.observation: balloon-catheter image (camera, segmentation-based 3D balloon tracking; Aurora as ground truth: within 3 mm, 3.6 ms per frame)
studies.action_space: discrete: translate 5 mm, rotate left or right 20 deg, stop
studies.gap_closing: patient-specific digital twin with calibrated material; twin vs real interaction compared in Fig. 2(b); deviations under 5 mm called non-critical
studies.real_setup: three water-filled patient-specific right-heart phantoms, static and pulsatile heartbeat, 50 autonomous interventions per phantom, 10 expert operations per heartbeat rate
studies.sim_success: N.R. (twin used to generate data, no sim success rate)
studies.real_success: >= 96% static, >= 94% dynamic; trajectory consistency >= 34.63% better than expert
studies.gap_measure: twin-vs-real interaction compared qualitatively (Fig. 2b) and by deviation (<5 mm criterion); no matched sim-vs-real success pair
studies.read_level: full (text; table 1 is an image, not read)
studies.notes: Missed by S7b. Cardiac, imitation-style transfer from digital twin, not RL. Roller drive with silicone layers is the one drive element named in a twin paper, but the twin imposes motion directly. Paper lists Karstensen 2022, Mei, Scarponi 2024, Robertshaw IRL, CathSim as related sim-to-real work.
